purpose: Levomilnacipran is used to treat major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults. It helps improve your mood, energy levels, sleep, appetite, and overall interest in daily life. Your doctor prescribed it to help you feel more like yourself again.
how_it_works: Your brain uses natural chemicals called serotonin and norepinephrine to help regulate your mood. When these chemicals run low, depression can set in. Levomilnacipran works by blocking the brain from reabsorbing these chemicals too quickly, so they stay active longer and help lift your mood.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, constipation, increased sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, and trouble sleeping are the most common side effects. Some men may notice difficulty urinating or delayed ejaculation. Most side effects are mild and often improve after the first few weeks.
warnings: Do not take this medication with MAO inhibitors as this can cause a dangerous reaction. It may increase blood pressure and heart rate, so your doctor will monitor these. There is a risk of increased suicidal thoughts, especially in young adults under 25, particularly when first starting the medication — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 20 mg once daily for the first two days, then increased to 40 mg once daily. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose up to a maximum of 120 mg once daily based on how you respond. Always take it at the same time each day and swallow the capsule whole — do not crush or chew it.
